definition: Lost motion in mechanical systems due to clearances between components (measured in mm or inches). Target: <0.05mm for precision CNC. Anti-backlash compensation: ball screw preload, spring-loaded nuts.
Precision lead screw using recirculating ball bearings to convert rotary to linear motion with high efficiency (90-95%) and low backlash (<0.01mm). Grades: C10 (±52μm/300mm) to C2 (±8μm/300mm).

Angular Contact: High-speed spindle bearings with contact angle 15-40°. Preload required. Deep Groove Ball: General-purpose radial/thrust bearing. Most common type. Tapered Roller: Heavy radial and thrust loads. Used in large gantries. Linear Ball Bearing: Recirculating ball bearing for linear motion on hardened shafts.
Beam supported at one end only. Z-axis spindle head is cantilever load. Deflection = FL³/(3EI).
Inverse of stiffness (μm/N). Higher compliance = more deflection under load.
Damping ratio ζ=1. System returns to equilibrium without oscillation. Under-damped: ζ<1 (oscillates), Over-damped: ζ>1 (slow return).
Reference surface, line, or point from which measurements are made. Critical for alignment and repeatability. Kinematic datum: 3-2-1 constraint principle (6 DOF constraint).
Number of independent motions. Rigid body: 6 DOF (3 translation + 3 rotation). CNC mill: 3 DOF (XYZ), 5-axis: 5 DOF.
Load capacity of bearing/guide that allows 1 million meters of travel (or 1 million revolutions for rotary bearings) before fatigue failure (90% reliability, L10 life).
Material stiffness (stress/strain ratio). Steel: 200 GPa, Aluminum: 69 GPa, Cast Iron: 100-140 GPa.
Tensile force applied during bolt tightening. Prevents joint separation and improves fatigue life. Target: 75-90% of proof load.
Bridge structure spanning machine bed, carrying Y-axis and Z-axis. Types: open (one rail) vs. closed (two rails). Closed gantry: better torsional rigidity.
Lag between input and output in mechanical systems. Ball screw hysteresis: <2μm typical. Caused by micro-slip in contacts.
Resistance to rotational acceleration. I = mr² for point mass. Critical for motor sizing and resonance analysis.
Width of material removed by cutting process. Plasma: 1-3mm, Fiber Laser: 0.1-0.5mm, Waterjet: 0.5-1.5mm, Router: tool diameter + deflection.
Exact-constraint mounting using 3 spheres on 3 V-grooves (or equivalents). Provides repeatable positioning <1μm. Used in precision fixtures.
Linear travel per revolution of screw. Ball screw: 5mm, 10mm, 20mm typical. Lead ≠ pitch for multi-start screws.
Precision bearing system with hardened rail and ball-bearing carriage. Accuracy: ±5-15μm over 300mm. Load ratings: 5-200 kN.
Dynamic (C): For moving loads, L10 life calculation. Static (C₀): Maximum load at standstill without permanent deformation. Moment Loads (M): Torque about carriage axes. Causes premature wear.
Frequency at which structure vibrates freely. fn = (1/2π)√(k/m). Avoid excitation near fn (resonance amplification).
Distance between screw threads. Ball screw: pitch × starts = lead. Rack & pinion: pitch circle diameter/# teeth.
Internal force applied to bearing or screw to eliminate clearance and increase stiffness. Ball screw: 3-7% of dynamic load. Linear guide: light/medium/heavy preload options.
Linear drive converting pinion rotation to rack translation. Module 1.5-3mm typical. Backlash: 0.1-0.3mm (larger than ball screw).
Ability to return to same position. Spec: ±10μm typical for CNC. Better than accuracy (absolute position error).
Minimum increment of motion. Encoder: 0.1-1μm typical. Stepper: microstep size (e.g., 1/8 step = 0.025mm for 5mm lead).
Total Indicator Reading - maximum deviation of rotating component from true circular path. Spindle target: <5 μm TIR at nose. Collet runout: <10 μm.
Maximum load bearing/guide can support without permanent deformation (0.0001× bearing diameter deformation criterion).
Resistance to deflection under load, measured in N/μm. Higher = better precision under cutting forces. System stiffness: series springs (1/ktotal = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂ + ...).
Maximum deviation from true straight line over specified length. Linear rail: 20μm/m typical. Measured with autocollimator or laser interferometer.
Load path from cutting tool to workpiece through machine structure. Shorter/stiffer loop = higher rigidity and accuracy.
Dimensional change due to temperature. Aluminum: 23.6 μm/(m·°C). Critical for precision machines - requires thermal compensation or cooling.
Squaring spindle axis perpendicular to table. Indicator sweep method. Target: <0.01mm over 300mm diameter.
Resistance to twisting under torque. Hollow tube 4-8× better than solid shaft of same weight. Critical for gantry beams.
High-frequency vibration of unsupported screw section. Occurs above critical speed: Ncrit = (4.76 × 10⁶ × d) / L² (RPM, mm). Requires center support.
Brushless motor with encoder feedback for closed-loop control. Higher power density than steppers. Typical: 0.1-15 kW per axis.
Position sensor providing unique code for each position. Retains position after power loss. Resolution: 17-25 bit (130k-33M positions/rev).
DC link voltage in servo drive (rectified AC). Typically 300-400V DC from 230V AC, 600-800V DC from 480V AC.
Switching current between motor windings to produce rotation. Stepper: external drive. Servo: internal with encoder feedback (field-oriented control).
Innermost control loop in servo drive. Bandwidth: 1-3 kHz. Controls motor torque proportional to commanded current.
Percentage of time component operates vs. rests. Servo peak torque: 30s duty cycle typical (3× continuous). Intermittent: cycles <10 min.
Ability of equipment to operate without EM interference. CE marking requires EMC testing per IEC 61000 series.
Unwanted electromagnetic radiation from electrical components interfering with signals. Mitigation: shielded cables, star grounding, ferrites, filters.

Incremental: Outputs A/B pulses (position change). Requires homing. Z-index pulse per revolution. Typical: 2500-10,000 PPR. Absolute: Direct position reading. Battery-backed or multi-turn (magnetic gearing). 17-bit = 131,072 counts/rev = 0.0027°. Resolver: Analog rotary transformer. Robust but low resolution. Used in harsh environments.
Real-time Ethernet protocol for motion control. 1000 axes at 1 kHz cycle time. Beckhoff, Delta, many drives support.
Advanced servo algorithm controlling flux and torque independently. Enables maximum torque/amp efficiency.

Connecting electrical circuits to earth potential. Types: Safety Ground: Green/yellow wire, protects against shock. Signal Ground: Common reference for signals. Star topology prevents ground loops. Chassis Ground: Frame/enclosure ground. Bonds to safety ground.
Magnetic position sensor. Used for commutation in brushless motors (3 sensors, 60° apart). Binary output.
Maximum torque stepper motor can produce at standstill (0 RPM). Decreases with speed (torque curves).
See Encoder (Incremental). Requires limit switch homing on power-up. More common than absolute (lower cost).
Opposition to current change in coil. Motor inductance: 1-50 mH. Limits acceleration capability (voltage = L × di/dt).
Initial surge current when powering equipment. Servo drive: 20-100× steady-state. Requires soft-start or pre-charge resistor.
Galvanic separation using LED/phototransistor. Isolates sensitive circuits from high-voltage/noisy circuits. Typical: 2500V isolation.
Rate of acceleration change (m/s³). High jerk causes vibration. S-curve acceleration profiles limit jerk for smooth motion.
Delay between command and response. Motion control: <1ms required. Ethernet latency: 0.1-1ms depending on protocol.
Dividing motor full steps into smaller increments (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32, 1/64, 1/128). Smoother motion but lower torque and positional accuracy at high microstep ratios.
Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor. Fast switching device in motor drives. Low on-resistance (Rdson: 5-50 mΩ).
See Isolation (Optical). Protects control circuits from motor noise and voltage spikes.
Proportional-Integral-Derivative feedback controller. Standard servo tuning: Kp (position gain), Ki (integral - removes steady-state error), Kd (derivative - damping).
Outermost servo control loop. Bandwidth: 10-100 Hz. Compares commanded vs. actual position (encoder), outputs velocity command.
Ratio of real power to apparent power. Inductive loads (motors): 0.6-0.9 typical. Unity (1.0) is ideal. VFDs improve power factor.
Motor drive technique varying duty cycle to control average voltage/current. Frequency: 4-20 kHz typical (above audible range).
Converting motor kinetic energy back to electrical energy during deceleration. Requires braking resistor (dissipate) or bus sharing (return to supply).
See Encoder (Resolver). Analog rotary position sensor. Rugged but requires resolver-to-digital converter (RDC) chip.
Effective value of AC waveform. Motor continuous ratings in RMS amps/volts. Peak = √2 × RMS for sine wave.
Closed-loop motor system with encoder feedback for precise position/velocity control. Corrects for disturbances (cutting forces, friction).
Conductive layer around cable preventing EM radiation. Braid (80-95% coverage) or foil (100% coverage). Ground shield at ONE end only (avoid ground loops).
Difference between synchronous speed and actual speed in AC induction motors. 2-5% at full load. Servo motors: zero slip (synchronous).
Open-loop motor moving in discrete steps. Holding torque: 0.3-30 N·m. Steps/rev: 200 (1.8°) or 400 (0.9°) typical. Loses steps if overloaded.
Vds: Drain-source voltage rating (e.g., 600V MOSFET). Ids: Continuous drain current (e.g., 50A MOSFET). Rdson: On-resistance (e.g., 10 mΩ = 0.5W at 10A).
Calculation of position/velocity/acceleration profiles. Trapezoidal profile: constant accel/decel. S-curve: limited jerk.
Adjusting PID gains for optimal servo response. Manual (Ziegler-Nichols, Lambda), Auto-tune (drive feature). Goal: fast settling without overshoot.
Middle servo control loop. Bandwidth: 100-500 Hz. Compares commanded vs. actual velocity (encoder derivative), outputs current command.
Electronic controller varying AC motor speed by adjusting frequency and voltage (V/Hz control). Spindle control: 0-400 Hz = 0-24,000 RPM.
Coordinates specified relative to fixed origin (work zero). Example: G90 G01 X100 → move to X=100.
G02 (CW) or G03 (CCW) circular path. Parameters: I/J (center offset) or R (radius). Requires XY plane (G17).
Mechanism swapping tools automatically. Carousel type: 8-40 tools. Arm type: 10-20s tool change. ISO 30/40/50 taper.
Primary (X, Y, Z): Linear translation axes. Z typically vertical (spindle axis). Right-hand rule. Rotary (A, B, C): Rotation about X, Y, Z respectively. 4th axis: rotary table. 5-axis: A+C or B+C.
Pre-programmed routines for common operations. G81 (drilling), G83 (peck drilling), G84 (tapping), G73 (high-speed peck).

Tool Length (G43): Offset Z position by tool length in table. G43 H01 = use tool 1 length. Tool Radius (G41/G42): Offset path left/right by tool radius. Climb milling: G41. Conventional: G42. Backlash Compensation: Software correction for mechanical backlash. LinuxCNC: [AXIS0]BACKLASH parameter.
Difference between commanded and actual position during motion. Servo: <0.1mm typical. Exceeding limit triggers alarm.
Machine (G53): Absolute position relative to home switches. Fixed reference. Work (G54-G59): User-defined origins for parts. G54 most common. G10 L2 sets offsets.
Test mode running program at reduced speed without tool engaged. Verify program before cutting.
CAD file format. 2D vector graphics. Common CAM input format for plasma/laser/waterjet.
Speed of tool movement through material (mm/min or in/min). Programmed with F-word. Higher = faster machining but more tool wear. Inverse time (G93) for 5-axis.
Material removed per cutter tooth. Formula: fz = F / (N × RPM) where F=feedrate, N=# teeth. Aluminum: 0.05-0.15 mm/tooth.
Machine programming language (RS-274). G00 (rapid), G01 (linear), G02/G03 (arc), G90/G91 (absolute/incremental).
LinuxCNC real-time software layer connecting G-code to hardware. Configuration: .hal files. Signals: bit/float/s32/u32 types.
Limit switch establishing machine origin. Homing sequence: rapid to switch, slow off switch, zero position. Index pulse optional (repeatable to 0.1μm).
Coordinates specified relative to current position. Example: G91 G01 X10 → move 10mm from current X.
CNC calculating intermediate points between programmed endpoints. Linear (G01): straight line. Circular (G02/G03): arc. NURBS: complex curves.
Calculating joint positions for desired tool position. Required for robotic arms, delta robots. LinuxCNC: genserkins, pumakins.
Manual axis movement via buttons/handwheel. Continuous (hold button) or incremental (0.001", 0.01", 0.1" steps).
Controller analyzing upcoming G-code to optimize velocity. Prevents overshoot at corners. Depth: 100-1000 segments typical.
Auxiliary machine functions (not motion). M03 (spindle CW), M08 (coolant on), M06 (tool change), M30 (program end).
Absolute position relative to machine home (physical limits). G53 ignores work offsets. Used for tool changes, safe positions.
Keyboard entry of single G-code commands. Useful for setup, probing, jogging to position.
Command remains active until cancelled. G01 (linear mode), G90 (absolute mode). Non-modal: G04 (dwell), G28 (home).

Work Coordinate (G54-G59): Part origin locations. G10 L2 P1 X10 Y20 = set G54 to X+10, Y+20. Tool Length (G43): Z compensation for tool length. Measured from gage line to tool tip. Tool Diameter (G41/G42): Radius compensation around programmed path.
Real-time adjustment of programmed values. Feed override: 0-200% typical. Spindle override: 50-120%. Lets operator fine-tune.
Using variables in G-code. #1=10 (assignment), G01 X#1 (use variable). Loops with WHILE, conditionals with IF.
Software converting CAM toolpaths to machine-specific G-code. Custom posts for each control (Fanuc, Haas, LinuxCNC, Mach3).
Precision switch for automatic workpiece/tool measurement. Renishaw: repeatability 0.5μm. G38.2 (probe toward), G38.4 (probe away).
M00 (mandatory stop), M01 (optional stop - requires operator enable). Spindle/coolant off, requires cycle start to continue.
Non-cutting move at maximum feedrate. Not guaranteed straight line (may move axes sequentially). No F-word.
System guaranteeing response within specified time. LinuxCNC: 1ms servo cycle, 25μs base thread (steppers). RTAI or Preempt-RT kernel.
Proportionally increase/decrease programmed dimensions. G51 X2 Y2 = double size. G50 cancels. Useful for families of parts.
Execution mode pausing after each G-code line. Used for program verification and debugging.
Coordinating spindle rotation with linear motion. Rigid tapping (G33.1): spindle encoder required. Thread milling: G02/G03 with helical interpolation.
Reusable G-code block called with M98 P1234 (call program O1234). M99 returns. Useful for repeated patterns (bolt holes).
Compensation for tool length/diameter differences. Length offset (G43): Z-axis. Radius compensation (G41/G42): XY plane. Stored in tool table.
Database of tool dimensions. Tool # (T), length offset (H), diameter (D), pocket (P). G10 L1 sets values. G43 H01 applies tool 1 length.
Calculates smooth motion profiles respecting velocity/acceleration limits. Acceleration: 0.5-5 m/s² typical. Jerk limiting optional.
User-defined origin for part coordinates. G54 most common (work offset 1), allows multiple fixtures/setups. Extended: G54.1 P1-P9 (G59.3).
Waterjet with garnet abrasive (80 mesh typical). Cuts metals, stone, ceramics. Pressure: 55,000-90,000 PSI. Kerf: 0.8-1.5mm.
CAM toolpath maintaining constant tool engagement. Varies feedrate and stepover for consistent chip load. Reduces tool wear 30-50%.
Material welding to tool edge at low speeds. Causes poor finish and tool failure. Solution: increase speed or use coated tools.
Removing chips from cutting zone. Methods: flood coolant (washing), air blast, vacuum, chip conveyor. Poor evacuation causes recutting and heat.
Thickness of chip removed per tooth. Formula: Chipload = Feed / (RPM × # teeth). Aluminum roughing: 0.10-0.20 mm/tooth. Finishing: 0.03-0.08 mm/tooth.

Self-excited vibration causing poor surface finish and tool breakage. Frequency: 100-5000 Hz. Causes: low rigidity, excessive DOC/WOC, tool runout. Solutions: reduce DOC, change RPM, increase rigidity.
Cutter rotation direction matches feed direction. Chip thickness: thick to thin. Advantages: better finish, lower forces, longer tool life. Requires backlash elimination.
Cutter rotation opposes feed direction. Chip thickness: thin to thick. Advantages: works with backlash. Disadvantages: lifts workpiece, more tool wear.
Fluid for cooling tool and workpiece. Types: water-soluble (emulsion, 5-20:1 dilution), synthetic, straight oil, MQL. Functions: cooling, lubrication, chip evacuation.
Tool radius offset (G41/G42). Programming to part edge, controller offsets by tool radius. Enables tool wear compensation without reprogramming.
Resistance of material to cutting. Components: tangential (Ft), radial (Fr), axial (Fa). Ft = Ks × DOC × WOC × fz^n (specific cutting force Ks from tables).
Velocity at tool cutting edge. Formula: Vc = π × D × N where D=diameter (mm), N=RPM. Steel: 100-300 m/min HSS, 150-500 m/min carbide.
Axial depth tool enters material. Symbol: ap. Roughing: 3-10mm or 50-100% of tool diameter. Finishing: 0.1-0.5mm.
Material removal by electrical sparks. Wire EDM: 0.1-0.3mm wire cuts intricate shapes. Sinker EDM: shaped electrode. Surface finish: 0.1-3μm Ra.
Feed rate (mm/min or IPM) and spindle speed (RPM) for specific material/tool combination. Calculate from chipload, # teeth, cutting speed.
Device holding workpiece during machining. Types: vise, toe clamps, vacuum table, custom (3-2-1 locating). Rigidity critical - workpiece stiffness > machine stiffness.
High-volume coolant delivery (5-50 GPM). Nozzles at tool-workpiece interface. Removes heat and chips. Requires sump, pump, filtration.
Crushed mineral for abrasive waterjet cutting. Mesh size: 50 (coarse), 80 (standard), 120 (fine). Cost: $0.10-$0.30/lb. Consumption: 0.3-1.0 lb/min.
Region near cut edge with altered microstructure. Plasma/laser: 0.5-2mm HAZ. Waterjet/router: zero HAZ (cold cutting).
Cutting at 5-10× conventional speeds. Aluminum: 15,000-30,000 RPM. Steel: 8,000-15,000 RPM. Requires rigid machine, balanced tools, high-performance spindle.
Width of material removed by cutting process. Compensation: program 0.5× kerf inside (internal features) or outside (external features).
Ramp or arc entry/exit to cut to avoid plunge marks. Circular lead-in: radius 1-5mm. Helps tool engagement and surface finish.
Volume of material removed per unit time. MRR = DOC × WOC × Feed (mm³/min). Roughing: maximize MRR. Finishing: minimize (better surface).
Micro-mist lubrication (0.01-0.1 mL/hr oil + air). Replaces flood coolant. Benefits: dry chips (recyclable), no disposal, cleaner. Aluminum, cast iron applications.
Arranging parts on material sheet to minimize waste. CAM nesting software. Common spacing: 3-10mm between parts (avoid thermal effects in plasma/laser).
Initial penetration of material before cutting. Plasma: 2-5 seconds pierce time, height above work (pierce height = 2× cut height). Laser: oxygen assist for thick steel.
P = (Ks × DOC × WOC × Feed) / (60 × η) where Ks=specific cutting force (N/mm²), η=efficiency (0.7-0.9). Steel: 0.5-10 kW typical.
Percentage of cutter diameter engaged in material. Full slot: 100%. Half slot: 50%. Light finish: 10-30%. Affects cutting forces and tool life.
High-MRR material removal leaving finishing stock. Larger DOC/WOC, faster feed, 0.1-0.5mm stock remaining. Surface finish: 3-10 μm Ra.
Residual cusps between toolpath passes. Smaller stepover = smaller scallop. Formula: h = stepover² / (8R) for ball end mill radius R.
See Feeds and Speeds. Critical for tool life and surface finish. Too fast: excessive heat/wear. Too slow: built-up edge, poor finish.
Cutting speed at tool edge (imperial). Formula: SFM = (π × D × RPM) / 12 (D in inches). Metric equivalent: Vc (m/min).
Lateral offset between toolpath passes. Percentage of tool diameter. Roughing: 40-60%. Finishing: 5-20%. Smaller = better finish, longer cycle time.
Arithmetic average roughness. Typical: Roughing 3-10 μm, General 0.8-3 μm, Precision 0.2-0.8 μm, Grinding <0.2 μm. Measured with profilometer.
High-pressure coolant (50-100 PSI) through hollow spindle and tool. Essential for deep hole drilling (>3× diameter). Rotary union seals coolant to rotating spindle.
Circular toolpath with advancing motion. Maintains small radial engagement (10-20%). Benefits: longer tool life, higher MRR in hard materials, deeper cuts.
Radial depth (stepover in one pass). Symbol: ae. Slotting: 100% diameter. Roughing: 40-60% diameter. Finishing: 10-30% diameter.
Material surface hardening from plastic deformation. Austenitic stainless (304/316): severe work hardening. Requires positive rake tools and adequate feedrates (avoid rubbing).
Metal mixture improving properties. Steel: C + Fe + Mn/Cr/Ni. Aluminum: 6061 (Mg+Si), 7075 (Zn). Properties vary widely by composition.
Heat treatment reducing hardness and internal stress. Process: heat to 700-900°C, slow cool. Makes material easier to machine.
FCC crystal structure of iron (stable above 912°C). Non-magnetic. Retained in stainless 304/316 (austenitic stainless).
WC particles in Co binder. Hardness: 1500-2000 HV (vs. 800 HV HSS). Cutting tools: grades C1-C8 (ISO K, M, P). Brittle but heat-resistant.
Surface hardening via carburizing/nitriding. Hard exterior (50-62 HRC), tough core (30-40 HRC). Gears, bearing races.
Fe-C alloy with 2-4% carbon. Types: Gray (graphite flakes, good damping), Ductile (nodular graphite), White (cementite, very hard). Machinable without coolant.
BCC crystal structure of iron (stable <912°C). Soft, magnetic. Pure iron mostly ferrite at room temperature.
Crystal size in material. Finer grain = stronger (Hall-Petch effect). Coarse grain: easier to machine but weaker. ASTM grain size number: 5-8 typical.
Resistance to deformation. Scales: Rockwell (HRC 20-65), Brinell (HB 100-650), Vickers (HV 100-1000). Conversion tables available. Harder materials require lower feeds/speeds.
Controlled heating/cooling altering microstructure. Types: annealing (soften), normalizing (refine grain), quenching (harden), tempering (toughness).
Tool steel with W, Mo, Cr, V. Hardness: 62-65 HRC. Cutting tools: drills, taps, end mills. Lower cost than carbide but lower heat resistance.
Hard, brittle phase formed by rapid quenching steel from austenite. BCT structure. 58-65 HRC typical. Requires tempering to reduce brittleness.
Strengthening via precipitate formation. Aluminum 6061-T6: Mg₂Si precipitates. Stainless 17-4PH: copper precipitates. Age hardening process.
Rapid cooling from austenite temperature forming martensite. Media: water (fastest, cracking risk), oil (moderate), air (slow). Hardness depends on cooling rate.
Hardness scale using diamond cone indenter. HRC 20 (mild steel), HRC 30-40 (prehardened steel), HRC 50-60 (hardened steel, cutting tools). Converted to HB, HV.

Fe-Cr alloy (>10.5% Cr) forming passive oxide layer. Types: Austenitic (304, 316): Non-magnetic, corrosion-resistant, work-hardens severely. Difficult to machine. Ferritic (430): Magnetic, less corrosion resistance, easier to machine. Martensitic (410, 420): Hardenable, magnetic, moderate corrosion resistance.
Designation of aluminum heat treatment. T6: solution treated + artificially aged (peak strength). T4: solution treated + naturally aged. O: annealed (soft).
Reheating quenched steel to reduce brittleness and stress. Temperature: 150-650°C. Higher temp = softer but tougher. Required after quenching to avoid cracking.
Heat transfer rate. Aluminum: 205 W/(m·K), Steel: 50 W/(m·K), Stainless: 15 W/(m·K). Higher = better coolant effectiveness, less thermal damage.
Energy absorption before fracture. Opposite of brittleness. Charpy/Izod impact tests. Tempered martensite: tough. Untempered martensite: brittle.
Maximum stress before failure. Mild steel: 400 MPa. 4140 steel: 655 MPa (annealed) to 1800 MPa (quenched). Design safety factor: 2-4×.
Stress causing permanent deformation (0.2% offset). Design limit for structures. Mild steel: 250 MPa. Aluminum 6061-T6: 276 MPa. Factor of safety applied.
Explosive electrical fault creating plasma arc. Energy: up to 40 cal/cm² (lethal). Protection: arc-rated PPE, proper clearances, lockout/tagout.
Standards organization. B11 series: machine tool safety. Z87.1: eye protection. Z49.1: welding safety.
EU declaration of conformity to safety directives. Required for machinery sold in Europe. Self-certification or notified body assessment.
Area with limited egress and not designed for continuous occupancy. Sump, tank interiors. OSHA 1910.146: permit required, atmosphere testing, rescue plan.
Two independent layers of insulation protecting against shock. Class II equipment (no ground required). Symbol: square within square.

Immediately removes power to motion/spindle. Required by ISO 13850 on all machines. Type: Category 0 (uncontrolled stop) or Category 1 (controlled stop then power off). Red mushroom button with yellow background.
Three-position switch for pendant operation. Squeezed: machine enabled. Fully pressed or released: machine disabled. Prevents unintended motion.
Arrest system for work >4 feet height (OSHA). Full-body harness + lanyard + anchor. Machine access platforms require guardrails or personal fall arrest.
Detects current imbalance (leakage to ground) and trips circuit. 5 mA threshold, <25ms trip time. Required for temporary/outdoor 120V circuits.
Physical barrier preventing access to hazards. Fixed (permanent), interlocked (door switch), adjustable. ANSI B11.19 specifies distances and openings.
Systematic identification of dangers. Risk = Severity × Probability. ISO 12100 risk assessment. Mitigation hierarchy: eliminate, guard, warn, train, PPE.
Safety device preventing machine operation unless conditions met (door closed, guards in place). Positive opening (mechanically driven to open state). Monitored by safety relay/PLC.
Global standards body. ISO 12100: machinery safety principles. ISO 13849-1: safety control systems. ISO 13850: emergency stop.
Optical safety device creating invisible barrier. 14mm spacing between beams typical. Safety category 2 or 4. Response time: 10-30ms. Replaces physical guarding.
Procedure isolating energy sources during maintenance (OSHA 1910.147). Lock device on disconnects, tags identifying worker. De-energize, dissipate stored energy, verify zero energy.
See Guarding. OSHA 1910.212 general requirements. Point of operation guarding: distance to hazard vs. opening size tables (1/4" opening = 4" distance minimum).
Fire safety standards. NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code), NFPA 79 (Industrial Machinery Electrical Standard), NFPA 654 (Combustible Dust).
US workplace safety enforcement. 29 CFR 1910: General Industry standards. 1910.212: machine guarding, 1910.147: LOTO, 1910.1000: air contaminants.
Maximum airborne concentration of substance allowed (OSHA). Oil mist: 5 mg/m³ (8-hr TWA). Hexavalent chromium (welding stainless): 5 μg/m³.
ISO 13849-1 safety reliability rating. PLa (lowest) to PLe (highest). PLd/PLe: redundant channels, diagnostics, fault tolerance. Emergency stops: typically PLd.
Safety gear required for operation. Hierarchy: last resort (engineering controls preferred). Minimum CNC: Z87.1 safety glasses, hearing protection >85 dB, steel-toe boots.
European term for GFCI. 30 mA threshold typical for personnel protection. 300 mA for equipment protection (fire prevention).
Evaluating hazard severity and probability. ISO 12100 methodology. Risk matrix: severity (1-4) × probability (1-4) = risk (1-16). Acceptable risk: <6 typical.

IEC 60204-1 classification of emergency stop reliability. Category 0: uncontrolled stop (immediate power removal). Category 1: controlled stop, then power removal. Category 2: controlled stop, power maintained.
IEC 61508 classification of safety system reliability. SIL 1 (10⁻¹ to 10⁻² failure probability) to SIL 4 (10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁴). Industrial machinery: typically SIL 2.
Redundant relay module monitoring safety circuits. Dual-channel inputs, force-guided contacts (mechanically linked NO/NC). Pilz, Phoenix Contact manufacturers.
Operator must use both hands on buttons to activate machine. Prevents hands in hazard zone. Anti-tie-down: buttons <300mm apart, must press within 0.5s.
Closeness of measurement to true value. Specification: ±10 μm/300mm typical for CNC. Systematic error (calibrated out with compensation).
Optical instrument measuring angular deviation. Resolution: 0.1 arc-second (0.5 μm/m). Leveling precision machines, measuring spindle axis alignment.
Comparison to known standard. Traceable to NIST/NPL national standards. Period: annual for production equipment, quarterly for metrology. Adjustment if out of tolerance.
Precision measurement device with touch probe on 3-axis gantry. Accuracy: 2-5 μm typical. Temperature-controlled room (20°C ±1°C).
Contact probe with 0.001" (0.01mm) resolution. Long-range (1-3"), continuous dial. Used for setup, runout measurement, tramming spindle.
Precision thickness blades for measuring gaps. 0.001" (0.025mm) to 0.040" (1mm) typical set. Used for gap setting, workpiece leveling.
Precision length standard. Grade 0: ±0.05 μm, Grade 1: ±0.1 μm, Grade 2: ±0.2 μm. Wrung together to create exact lengths. Calibration reference.
Optical measurement using light wave interference. Accuracy: <1 ppm (1 μm/m). Renishaw XL-80 laser: 0.5 ppm linear accuracy. Machine tool calibration.
Precision screw-threaded measuring instrument. 0.001" (0.01mm) graduation, 0.0001" (0.001mm) vernier. Outside, inside, depth types. Thimble friction ratchet for consistent force.
Measurement error from viewing dial at angle. Avoided by perpendicular viewing or mirror scale (align pointer with reflection).
Repeatability of measurements (scatter). Standard deviation of repeated measurements. High precision with poor accuracy: systematic error (bias).
Ability to return to same position. Spec: ±10 μm typical for CNC. Better than accuracy (absolute position error). Critical for production machining.
Minimum increment of motion or measurement. Encoder: 0.1-1 μm typical. Stepper: microstep size. Display resolution ≠ accuracy.
Precision flat reference. Grade A: 50 μm/m, Grade AA: 15 μm/m. Camelback beam shape (self-weight sag compensation). Used with feeler gauges, height gauges.
Precision flat reference surface. Granite (Grade A, AA, AAA). Grade A: 25 μm over 600×900mm plate. Temperature-stable (20°C). Inspection and layout.
Horizontal plunger indicator with 0.0001"-0.001" graduation. Small contact point. Used for fine centering, edge finding, small radii.
Acceptable variation from nominal dimension. ±0.1mm typical. ISO 2768: general tolerances (fine, medium, coarse). Geometric tolerances: position, flatness, perpendicularity (GD&T).
Documented chain to national standards. Calibration certificate from NIST-accredited lab. Required for AS9100 aerospace, ISO 17025 metrology labs.
Secondary scale for interpolation between main scale graduations. 0.02mm or 0.001" resolution typical. Used on calipers, height gauges, protractors.
See Waterjet terminology. Garnet cutting hard materials (steel, titanium, stone, glass).
Gas flow during laser cutting improving quality and speed. Oxygen (steel: exothermic oxidation), Nitrogen (stainless, aluminum: inert, no oxidation), Air (mild steel, budget option).
Laser beam spreading with distance. <0.1 mrad typical for fiber lasers. Affects focal position sensitivity and cut edge taper.
Electrode, nozzle, swirl ring, shield cap. Life: 1-4 hours piercing heavy plate, 10-50 hours cutting thin sheet. Cost: $5-$30 per set depending on amperage.
Nozzle standoff from workpiece. Plasma: 3-6mm (initial height controllers maintain). Laser: focal point at or below surface. Waterjet: 2-5mm (abrasive jet spread).
Solidified slag on cut edge underside. Plasma/laser: oxidized metal. Minimized by proper parameters (speed, gas flow, height). Removal: grinding, wire wheel.
Distance from laser lens to focal point. Common: 5" (127mm), 7.5" (190mm). Shorter = smaller spot, thinner material. Longer = more working distance, less sensitive.
See Machining Terms. Plasma: 1-2mm HAZ with hardness changes. Laser: 0.3-1mm HAZ. Waterjet: zero HAZ (cold process).
Leading plasma system manufacturer. PowerMax (handheld), Powermax (light duty), HPR (heavy duty). Market standard for CNC plasma.
See General terms. Plasma: 1-3mm depending on amperage (45A-200A). Laser: 0.1-0.5mm (1-6 kW fiber). Waterjet: 0.8-1.5mm (orifice + abrasive expansion).
Copper component focusing plasma arc. Orifice size: 0.8-2mm depending on amperage. Cools rapidly during cutting. Replace when orifice eroded >25%.
Sapphire or diamond jewel forming high-pressure water stream. Diameter: 0.010"-0.020" (0.25-0.50mm). Life: sapphire 50-100 hrs, diamond 800-2000 hrs.
Initial penetration before cutting. Plasma: 1-5 seconds at 1.5-2× cut height to avoid blowback. Laser: 0.1-2 seconds depending on power and thickness.
Laser power per unit area. 10⁶-10⁸ W/cm² for cutting. Higher = faster cutting speeds. Focused fiber laser: 10× CO₂ laser power density.
Lower-amperage arc stabilization before main arc transfer. 10-30A preheat. Improves arc starts and consumable life.
Angle deviation from vertical. Plasma: 0-3° typical. Laser: 0-2°. Waterjet: trailing edge (jet lag). Minimized by slow speeds and proper standoff.
Automated nozzle height adjustment during cutting. Capacitive sensor (non-contact) or arc voltage (plasma). Maintains constant height over warped sheets.
Main plasma cutting arc (vs. pilot arc). Workpiece completes electrical circuit. Higher efficiency than non-transfer arc (gouging).
Laser light wavelength. CO₂: 10.6 μm (infrared). Fiber/Nd:YAG: 1.06 μm (near-infrared). Fiber absorbed better by metals (higher cutting efficiency).
